Five studios compete for Port St. Lucie's dance students. None has finished the work AI search now rewards.

We audited 5 dance and ballroom studios serving the Port St. Lucie market head to head: site quality, Google's local results, and 6 live checks across ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI. The sites range from 65 to 76. The AI engines name only three of the 5. The field averages 69 (D) on AI readiness, 5 of 5 have no FAQ or Q&A structured data, and 3 of 5 have no llms.txt file. Whichever studio closes that gap first changes the answer for everyone searching this market.

Prepared by SiteTradeIn · Market snapshot generated 29 Oct 2026 · Independent audit — not commissioned by any studio in the field · See the ranked list

About this report

This is a market-wide snapshot, not an audit of a single business. We picked one competitive local market — dance and ballroom instruction in the Port St. Lucie, FL area — and ran the same measurement against every studio that competes for it: an automated site-quality grade across seven categories, where each studio shows up in Google's local results, and 6 live checks asking three AI engines who they'd recommend for two real buyer queries. Every studio named below is graded on identical criteria, on the same day, with no advance notice.

The point isn't to single any one studio out — it's to show what an AI-search-era competitive landscape actually looks like once you measure it instead of guessing at it. If your studio is one of the 5 below, this is where you stand today.

What the field shows

  • Fred Astaire Dance Studios Stuart (76) and Fred Astaire Dance Studios Port St. Lucie (73) lead on site quality, and the field runs down to 65. Every studio in the field still carries at least one D or F category.
  • No studio earns an A for AI readiness. The field averages 69 (D) on the category that decides whether an AI engine can read, trust and quote a site; the best score in the market is 77.
  • None of the 5 studios has FAQ or Q&A structured data, and 3 have no llms.txt file — the two cheapest AI-answer signals available. No studio in the market has both.
  • All 5 studios have images without alt text, from 14 of 52 images to 193 of 199 — easy points every site in the field is leaving on the table.
  • Two of the 5 are franchise locations (two Fred Astaire); the rest are independent studios.
  • The gap between #1 and #5 is 11 points on identical criteria. Nothing in the scorecard requires a rebuild or a rebrand to close it — just the work.

Two of the 5 studios are never named on any of the 6 checks: DanceSport Academy, Royal Ballroom Dance Studio. For a studio not doing this work, that's the default outcome — not a penalty, just the result of nobody in that seat having claimed it yet.

What separates the winners from the rest

  • Off-site proof, not just on-site polish. AI answers draw on what other sites say about a studio, not just on its own pages, so reviews, directory listings and a complete Google profile carry real weight.
  • Being unmistakably “in Port St. Lucie.” Studios that serve Port St. Lucie from nearby towns need pages, profiles and listings that say so in the words people search.
  • A complete, specific site. The strongest sites have no missing H1s or meta descriptions, alt text on their images, and schema that describes what the studio actually is. No studio in this field has all of that yet.
  • Content matched to how people actually ask. The broad question and the ballroom question pull from different result sets — a studio needs to answer both.

Methodology & notes

Field (5 studios): fredastaire.com/stuart-fl, fredastaire.com/port-st-lucie, astradancestudio.com, dancesportacademy.org, dancevero.com. Chosen from live Google searches on 29 Oct 2026: every adult ballroom, Latin or partner-dance studio with a working website that appeared in Google's local results for Port St. Lucie dance searches. Only five studios in these searches fit this field. ChatGPT named Jensen Beach Ballroom Dance Studio, which didn't appear in Google's local results for these searches. Gemini named Ballroom at Tradition and Jang & Adele DanceSport World, which didn't appear in Google's local results for these searches either. Left out: Seaside Dance Studio (its website announces the studio has closed, though Google's AI Mode names it), Craig's Dance Studio in Stuart (its domain no longer resolves), Ballroom Dancing by Susan Cosentino, Crystal Ballroom in Jensen Beach and Ballroom Dance Studio Iluna (no website of their own), Breath of Cuba and Latin Rhythms Dancing (no studio address on Google), and the youth, ballet and competition studios that lead the broad answers (South Florida Dance Company, True Crew Dance Company, Extreme Dance Company, Dance 4 Life Academy, St Lucie Dance Theatre, Tutu School).

Site audit: the same SiteTradeIn engine run for every studio on 29 Oct 2026, up to six pages per site, seven categories. Franchise locations that live on a national website (Fred Astaire) share that site's robots.txt, llms.txt, sitemap and templates.

AI visibility: 6 live checks — ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI, each asked “What are the best dance studios in Port St. Lucie, FL?” and “What are the best ballroom dance studios in Port St. Lucie, FL?” with a request for a top-five numbered list. Rankings are taken from each engine's own list; presence was confirmed by reading the raw response text, and every franchise mention was matched to its location. Each question was asked in a fresh session of each engine's web app (ChatGPT and Gemini logged out, Google's AI Mode), not through a developer API.

Google: local (Places) and first-page organic results captured in a live browser session on 29 Oct 2026 for “ballroom dance lessons port st lucie fl”; “dance lessons port st lucie fl”; “salsa lessons port st lucie fl”; “wedding dance lessons port st lucie fl”; “ballroom dance lessons stuart fl”, plus the organic searches “best dance studios in port st lucie fl” and “ballroom dance studio port st lucie”. Each query named the city; results vary by searcher location and over time.

Independence. This report is a market-wide measurement, not commissioned by or customized for any single studio named in it.

Limits. AI answers and search results vary between runs and over time; these are a point-in-time sample, not a fixed ranking.
